enums.name: WsError

variants.name: Refused

fields.name: status
fields.docs: The HTTP status of the refused upgrade, if the platform tells.

fields.name: message
fields.docs: What the platform said.

variants.docs:
The connection was not established. `status` is the HTTP status of the refused upgrade
where the platform reports it (browsers do not).

variants.name: Network
variants.docs: The connection failed or dropped without a closing handshake; the text is the platform's.

variants.name: Protocol
variants.docs: The peer broke the protocol (or a port reply did not decode); the text says how.

variants.name: Closed

fields.name: code
fields.docs: The close code (RFC 6455 §7.4): 1000 normal, 1001 going away, 1008 policy, ...

fields.name: reason
fields.docs: The close reason, possibly empty.

variants.docs: The connection was closed with a close frame: `code` and `reason` are the frame's.

enums.docs:
Why a WebSocket could not be opened, or how it ended (ADR-047 §5).

| What happened | Variant |
|---|---|
| the upgrade was answered non-101, the URL is unusable, headers the platform cannot send | `Refused` |
| the connection dropped without a close frame (DNS, reset, TLS, timeout) | `Network` |
| the peer broke RFC 6455, or a reply did not decode | `Protocol` |
| the peer sent a close frame (1000 included), or the adapter closed past its backlog limit (1008) | `Closed` |

ports.name: Db

methods.name: open
methods.docs:
Opens (creating it if needed) the database `name` and runs, in one transaction, every
migration above its `user_version`.

methods.name: execute
methods.docs: Runs one statement with `params` bound positionally; `db` is a database or transaction id.

methods.name: query
methods.docs: Runs one query with `params` bound positionally and returns every row.

methods.name: begin
methods.docs: Waits for any running transaction on `db`, starts one (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) and returns its id.

methods.name: commit
methods.docs: Commits transaction `tx` and ends it (a failed commit rolls back and ends it too).

methods.name: rollback
methods.docs: Rolls transaction `tx` back and ends it.

methods.name: close
methods.docs: Closes database `db` (a running transaction is rolled back). Closing twice is not an error.

ports.docs:
SQLite on the platform (ADR-048). Use [`Database`] rather than calling it directly.

Every open database has one connection and one serial worker owned by the adapter; the core
only awaits replies. Statements on a transaction id run inside it; statements on the database
id wait for a running transaction to end (at most the busy timeout, then `Busy`).

ports.name: Fs

methods.name: read
methods.docs: The contents of the file at `path`.

methods.name: write
methods.docs: Writes `data` to `path`, creating missing directories and replacing an existing file.

methods.name: delete
methods.docs: Removes the file or directory at `path`.

methods.name: list
methods.docs: The names of the entries directly inside `dir`, in ascending order.

ports.docs:
A sandboxed file system. Paths are `/`-separated and relative to the platform's root.

A platform without a file system answers "unavailable"; every method reports that as an
`FsError::Unavailable` through `impl From<PortError> for FsError` instead of panicking.

ports.name: Http

methods.name: request
methods.docs:
Performs `req`. Any status is a response; only failures before a response exists are an
`HttpError`.

ports.docs:
Performs HTTP requests.

A platform that did not register the port answers "unavailable"; `request` reports that (and a
cancelled call, and a reply that does not decode) as an `HttpError`, through
`impl From<PortError> for HttpError`, instead of panicking.

methods.name: delete

methods.name: list

ports.docs: A persistent key-value store of byte strings; every method can fail with a [`StorageError`].

methods.name: set

A key-value store for secrets. Same methods as `Kv`, under its own port id, and the same

ports.name: Sse

methods.name: open
methods.docs:
Requests `url` with `Accept: text/event-stream`, `headers` and, when given, the
`Last-Event-ID` header. Completes with the stream's id once a 2xx `text/event-stream`
answer arrived.

methods.name: next
methods.docs:
The next events, at least one and at most `max`, once there are any. `Ok([])` means the
core closed the stream; an error ends it.

methods.name: close
methods.docs:
Stops the stream and releases the connection; a pending `next` answers `Ok([])`.
Closing a stream that already ended is not an error.

ports.docs:
Opens server-sent event streams on the platform (ADR-047). Use [`subscribe`] rather than
calling it directly.

ports.name: Timer

methods.name: set
methods.docs: Arms timer `timer_id` to fire after `delay_ms` milliseconds.

ports.docs:
Arms timers. Fire-and-forget: the platform later reports `TimerFired(timer_id)` to the
runtime, which completes the matching sleep. Timer ids are allocated by the runtime; a
platform never invents one.

ports.name: WebSocket

methods.name: connect
methods.docs:
Opens a connection to `url` (`ws://` or `wss://`), offering `protocols` and sending
`headers` with the upgrade request. Completes once the handshake succeeded.

methods.name: send
methods.docs:
Sends `message`; completes when the platform accepted it and its outbound buffer is
under its high-water mark.

methods.name: receive
methods.docs:
The next messages, at least one and at most `max`, once there are any. `Ok([])` means
the core closed the connection; an error ends the inbound stream.

methods.name: close
methods.docs:
Starts the closing handshake with `code` and `reason`; a pending `receive` then answers
`Ok([])`. Closing a connection that already ended is not an error.

ports.docs:
Opens WebSocket connections on the platform (ADR-047). Use [`WsConnection`] rather than
calling it directly: it keeps the pull discipline and closes what it opened.

Every method has an error channel, so a platform without an adapter answers
`WsError::Network(..E0062..)` instead of panicking.

ports.name: Uploader
ports.docs: The platform uploads a request in the background.
